summary: The Kremlin floats a three-power summit on Ukraine, Houthi attacks cancel Riyadh's showcase, France brings in curfews, Japan heads for a Mars moon, and an AI lab hires fewer juniors.

topics.heading: Kremlin floats a Putin-Trump-Xi meeting on Ukraine; Kyiv objects to being left out
topics.summary: The Kremlin says Putin, Trump and Xi could meet at next month's APEC summit in China to discuss the war, though nothing is agreed. Ukraine's foreign minister says talks without Kyiv would only encourage Russia to keep fighting.

lead.title: Kremlin says Putin, Trump and Xi could hold a three-way meeting in China next month

alsoReported.title: Putin, Xi And Trump Could Meet At APEC Summit, Says Kremlin

article: On Monday, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said a three-way meeting between Vladimir Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping "came up" in talks and could happen at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen on November 18-19[^1][^2]. He stressed that no proposal, date or agenda has been agreed[^2]. The comments followed a Wall Street Journal report that Putin wants such a meeting to settle the war on terms that favour Moscow[^1].

Ukraine pushed back quickly. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha wrote that a meeting of Ukraine, the US and Russia could end the war sooner, but a Russia-China-US meeting would encourage Putin to keep fighting[^2]. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he did not know if anything was finalised but that Trump wants the war to end; China's foreign ministry said it had no information[^1].

Background: the last US-mediated peace talks were in February, before the US and Israel went to war with Iran, and Russia and Ukraine remain far apart on territory and guarantees[^2]. Peskov also said a final deal is impossible without someone in Kyiv who can take responsibility for it, which signals that Russia does not see a three-power meeting as a substitute for Ukraine's signature[^1][^2].

Why it matters: the meeting would take place on Chinese soil, with Ukraine absent. My read is that the idea tests whether great powers will try to decide Ukraine's future over its head, a worry for Kyiv and for Europe. Watch whether the White House accepts, and whether Ukraine is offered a seat.
topics.differences: The Kremlin presents the idea as a path to peace and says US mediation continues[^2]. Ukraine's foreign minister calls a meeting without Kyiv a reward for Russia[^2]. Washington has not committed, and Beijing says it has no information[^1].

topics.heading: Saudi Arabia postpones its flagship investment summit after Houthi attacks
topics.summary: The Future Investment Initiative, set for October 26-29 in Riyadh, is pushed to 2027 after Houthi missile and drone strikes, including on the capital's airport. Egypt's parliament delayed its vote on helping defend Saudi Arabia to October 26.

lead.title: Saudi Arabia postpones FII conference in Riyadh after Houthi attacks

alsoReported.title: Egyptian parliament delays vote on military support for Saudi Arabia

article: Saudi Arabia has postponed the 10th Future Investment Initiative, nicknamed "Davos in the Desert", which was due to bring global bankers such as BlackRock's Larry Fink and JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon to Riyadh next week[^3]. The organisers said it will now take place in 2027, with dates still to come[^3]. Two other business events in the kingdom were also moved[^3].

The reason is the war on Saudi Arabia's southern border. Yemen's Houthi movement, which is aligned with Iran, has stepped up missile and drone attacks on Saudi oil sites and on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport[^4][^5]. Saudi authorities say 13 people were killed in the October 10 airport attack[^4]. The fighting has grown since the US and Israel attacked Iran in February[^5].

Egypt is weighing whether to join in. Its National Defence Council approved a plan to support Saudi Arabia on Sunday, but parliament, which needs a two-thirds majority to send troops on a combat mission abroad, adjourned the vote to October 26[^4]. Analysts quoted by Reuters expect air-defence and naval help rather than ground troops in Yemen[^5]. Egypt depends on Gulf money and on Red Sea shipping through the Suez Canal, which the Houthis have disrupted since 2023[^4][^5].

Why it matters: the summit is a showcase for Saudi Arabia's plan to diversify away from oil, known as Vision 2030[^3]. Calling it off is a sign that the Iran war's side conflicts are now costing the Gulf economically, not only militarily. My read: the Egyptian vote next week is the next test of whether the war widens.

topics.heading: France imposes local curfews after a weekend of riots and looting
topics.summary: After protests over living costs and schools turned violent, France ordered night curfews in parts of Paris, Lille, Lyon and Nice. About 2,400 people were arrested over the weekend, and Macron refused his interior minister's resignation.

lead.title: France announces partial curfews after weekend of violence

alsoReported.title: France announces curfews in aftermath of violent protests

article: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu asked regional authorities to impose "partial" and "localised" curfews after two nights of looting and arson[^7]. In Paris, a curfew from 11 pm to 6 am covers areas around Place de la République and Les Halles, and demonstrations are banned in several areas at night; Lille and nearby towns have curfews Monday and Tuesday, and Nice has one for minors in its centre[^6][^7]. Lecornu said putting all of Paris under curfew is "out of the question"[^7].

The government says about 2,400 people were arrested over the weekend and almost 1,000 police and gendarmes were injured on Saturday; Lecornu called it "a miracle" that no one was killed[^6][^7]. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez admitted police "lost control" in some cities and offered to resign; President Emmanuel Macron refused and asked him for transparency about planning and intelligence failures[^6][^7].

The protests began with grievances many people share. Students have marched against crowded classrooms and teacher shortages, and others against the cost of living and weaker public services; more than half a million people joined Saturday's protests, most of them peacefully[^7]. Al Jazeera reports the violent weekend marches were led by the "yellow vest" movement, which has called more protests for Saturday[^7].

Why it matters: France votes for a new president in about six months, with a weak economy and rising debt[^7]. My read: how the government answers the underlying complaints, not only the riots, will shape that race.

topics.heading: Japan launches a mission to bring back the first samples from a moon of Mars
topics.summary: JAXA's Martian Moons eXploration spacecraft left Earth on an H3 rocket and is on course for Mars. It aims to land on the moon Phobos, collect samples and return them to Earth in 2031.

lead.title: Japan launches historic MMX sample-return mission to Mars' moon Phobos

alsoReported.title: JAXA's MMX Enroute to Mars To Return Samples of Phobos

article: Japan's space agency, JAXA, launched the Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) spacecraft from Tanegashima at 3:41 pm Toronto time on Monday (early Tuesday in Japan)[^8][^9]. About 71 minutes later it separated from the rocket on a path to Mars, where it should arrive in August 2027[^8].

MMX will not land on Mars itself. It will study Mars's two small moons, Phobos (about 22 km across) and Deimos, touch down on Phobos twice to collect about 10 grams of material, and drop a small rover called Idefix, built by France and Germany[^8][^9]. NASA supplied two instruments, including the sampler, and will receive a share of the sample[^8]. The capsule is due to land in Australia in 2031[^8][^9].

The science question is where these moons came from. One idea is that they are asteroids captured by Mars's gravity; another is that they formed from debris after something large hit Mars[^8][^9]. Phobos's near-circular orbit, lined up with Mars's equator, points toward the impact idea, but only a sample can settle it[^9]. If MMX succeeds, it would be the first sample brought back from any moon other than our own[^9].

Why it matters: Japan already returned asteroid samples with its Hayabusa missions, and this is a harder trip[^9]. Russia's 2011 attempt to reach Phobos failed in Earth orbit, a reminder that the hard parts are still ahead[^8].

topics.heading: An AI lab reports hiring far fewer junior technical staff as its AI agents take on work
topics.summary: Anthropic, the maker of the Claude AI models, published data on its own workforce: juniors fell from 27% to 9% of its technical hires, while total hiring grew. The authors stress that one unusual company is a limited guide.

lead.title: Is AI squeezing entry level tech jobs? Anthropic's junior technical hiring drops from 27% to 9%

article: Anthropic, one of the main US developers of AI models, released a study of how work has changed inside the company[^10]. Its researchers report that junior employees fell from 21% to 14% of technical staff since early 2025, and that juniors made up 9% of technical hires, down from 27%[^10][^11]. Overall headcount is still growing; the change is in the share of beginners, not layoffs[^11].

The report links this to AI agents, programs that carry out multi-step tasks on their own. It says agents directed by individual employees logged six times as many hours as the employees themselves by August, and code output per engineer rose about fivefold in six months[^10]. People also spend about 20% more time in meetings, partly to direct and check the AI's work[^10][^11].

The authors list real limits. Anthropic is a single, fast-growing AI company; the link between AI and junior hiring is described, not proven to be cause and effect; and much of the measurement was itself done by automated tools[^10]. They write that none of the company's own measures will prevent powerful AI from disrupting jobs, and call for government help with retraining and income support[^10]. (Note: this brief is written with help from an Anthropic model, so I have kept to the report's own figures and caveats.)

Why it matters: entry-level jobs are how most people learn a trade. If firms need fewer beginners, the path into careers like software could narrow. My read: this is one early data point from inside the industry, worth watching against wider job statistics.

topics.heading: Trump endorses Netanyahu nine days before Israel's election
topics.summary: Trump backed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for the October 27 vote, tying the choice to Iran. Netanyahu trails his main rival, former army chief Gadi Eisenkot, in recent polls, and Eisenkot asked for no foreign interference.

lead.title: Trump endorses Netanyahu ahead of Israeli elections, citing Iranian threat

alsoReported.title: Trump backs Netanyahu: Is the US planning a new Iran attack with Israel?

article: On Sunday, Donald Trump endorsed Benjamin Netanyahu on Truth Social, calling him a "great warrior prime minister" and saying the US would "soon finish the job" with Iran unless Tehran changed course[^13]. JTA reports Trump also said that if Israel chose another leader, the US would have to handle Iran itself[^12]. He had previously held back from endorsing anyone[^12].

Israelis vote on October 27. Netanyahu has trailed former army chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot in recent surveys[^12]. A seat tracker cited by Al Jazeera projects Eisenkot's opposition alliance at 52 of 120 seats and Netanyahu's coalition at 51, so neither would have a majority on its own[^13].

Reactions split along predictable lines. Eisenkot called Trump a great friend of Israel but said the vote is an internal matter[^12]. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, a Netanyahu ally, said Israel should listen to Trump[^12]. Iran's foreign minister said Iran has "unfinished jobs too" and repeated an offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if the US accepts its conditions[^13].

Why it matters: the next Israeli government will shape the stalled Gaza truce and any renewed war with Iran. Analysts quoted by Al Jazeera say the endorsement helps Netanyahu but cannot by itself build him a majority[^13]. This is a judgment, but the result may depend more on coalition arithmetic after the vote than on outside support.
topics.differences: Supporters, including Netanyahu's allies, frame the endorsement as a vote of confidence on Iran policy[^12]. Eisenkot and a US pro-Israel Democratic group see it as interference in a democratic election[^12]. Analysts disagree on how much it changes the odds of new strikes on Iran[^13].

question.text: An AI company published data about how AI is changing its own hiring. What would you want to know, and from whom, before deciding how much that tells you about the jobs waiting for your generation?
